summary: Receives Open Sound Control messages over UDP/multicast and exposes message values as CHOP channels with optional queuing and pulse behavior.
key_concepts: OSC In CHOP accepts Open Sound Control messages and exposes values as CHOP channels.
The OSC input is connection-less and can receive from multiple sources, but the configured port must be free before binding.
Protocol selects UDP messaging or multicast UDP messaging, with Network Address and Local Address controlling multicast/listen binding.
Queue parameters smooth incoming packet timing at the cost of latency and use explicit unit parameters for variance, maximum queue, and adjustment time.
OSC Address Scope filters received OSC address paths, and Strip Path Segments controls how address paths become channel names.
Pulse Mode and reset parameters help convert event-like OSC arrivals into transient CHOP channels.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Receive OSC messages on the configured port

key_params.name: adjusttime
key_params.note: Time allowed outside target queue range before adjustment

key_params.name: stripsegments
key_params.note: Strip address path segments from channel names

key_params.name: resetvalues
key_params.note: Reset channel values when no new OSC message is present

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: OSC CHOPs use UDP, so delivery/order is not guaranteed.
The listen port must not already be in use before OSC In binds it.
When Active is off, data sent to the port is lost rather than buffered.
Connection is source-agnostic; it can accept messages from multiple senders at the same time.
Pulse Mode is useful for detecting arrivals, but it reads a single sample then shows reset values otherwise.
On Windows, firewall settings are a common cause of connection failures.
Use OSC In DAT when the message structure/event stream is more important than continuous CHOP channels.
